pr_title: assert: partialDeepStrictEqual now handles comparisons of ArrayBuffers, SharedArrayBuffers and Int16Arrays
pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/56097

Added handling for ArrayBuffers, SharedArrayBuffers and Int16Arrays , which were not properly considered in the new method `assert.partialDeepStrictEqual` .  
This PR should move the feature one step closer to a stable version

issue_context.title: assert: partialDeepStrictEqual does not properly work comparing Int16Arrays, ArrayBuffers and SharedArrayBuffers
issue_context.body:
### Version

v24.0.0-pre

### Platform

```text
Darwin prot-2.local 24.1.0 Darwin Kernel Version 24.1.0: Thu Oct 10 21:05:23 PDT 2024; root:xnu-11215.41.3~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6031 arm64
```


### Subsystem

_No response_

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

Following what still needed to be done in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/54630 , I kept looking for discrepancies between what works with assert.deepStrictEqual and what should work with assert.partialDeepStrictEqual but it does not.

```js
const assert = require('assert');

assert.throws(() => assert.partialDeepStrictEqual(new ArrayBuffer(3), new SharedArrayBuffer(3)), Error);
assert.throws(() => assert.partialDeepStrictEqual(new Int16Array(3), new Uint16Array(3)), Error);
assert.partialDeepStrictEqual(new Int16Array([1, 2, 3]), new Int16Array([1, 2, 3]));
```

all the tests above will fail, while they should not

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

always

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

```js
const assert = require('assert');

assert.throws(() => assert.partialDeepStrictEqual(new ArrayBuffer(3), new SharedArrayBuffer(3)), Error);
assert.throws(() => assert.partialDeepStrictEqual(new Int16Array(3), new Uint16Array(3)), Error);
assert.partialDeepStrictEqual(new Int16Array([1, 2, 3]), new Int16Array([1, 2, 3]));
```

all the tests above will fail, while they should not

### What do you see instead?

the tests above will fail

### Additional information

_No response_

review_comments: Can you add a pair of `[new ArrayBuffer(3), new SharedArrayBuffer(3)]` and `[new SharedArrayBuffer(2), new ArrayBuffer(2)]` please?
all the relevant tests have been added to `test-assert-objects.js`, including the ones you just mentioned. But I can add them here too if you want
@aduh95 you are right, I missed one case! Updated, thanks 😄
I don't think this works with `DataView` objects, can you add a test?
